description:
FILED s532a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-01), found probing #4164.  PRE-EXISTING (base 10cdc985 identical).  SILENT (a failure perl reports is a success).

    open(B, "") ? print "e opened\n" : print "e failed $!\n";
    open(C, "<") ? print "c opened\n" : print "c failed $!\n";
  perl 5.40.3: e failed No such file or directory / c failed No such file or directory
  PCL: e opened / c opened

After #4164 an all-blank 2-arg name trims to "" and takes the same path.  Find what the runtime's open does with an empty file name (it opens something -- STDIN?) and make it fail with ENOENT as perl's PerlIO_open does.  Layer: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-open / %p-open-impl.  Probe: scratch/s532a/p/op2.pl.

=== DONE (s536h) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, commit 79b44e62, cl/ only).  %p-open-file now takes the perl NAME and answers an empty one with ENOENT for every mode (2-arg "", "<", ">", ">>", "+<", "   " after #4164's trim, 3-arg "<"/">"/">>"/"+<"/"+>" with "", the lexical autoviv shape) -- CL merged the empty pathname with the default directory, so a READ opened the CURRENT DIRECTORY and a write failed EISDIR.  The six file arms of %p-open-impl pass the name; %p-literal-path is applied inside.  Guard Pl/t/open-modes-01.t row 10 (12 shapes + "no file was created"; FAILS on the base).
subject: open(F, "") / open(F, "   ") / open(F, "<", "") SUCCEED in PCL -- perl fails them ENOENT (an empty file name)
